Yesterday, the U.S. government released an updated list of prohibited foreign-manufactured products, adding a new category for "advanced robotic devices." A Federal Communications Commission (FCC) spokesperson confirmed today that the ban also applies to robotic vacuum cleaners.

The robotic vacuum cleaner ban affects well-known brands such as Roomba and Roborock, but you can still continue using the products you already own

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the United States, media attention focused on humanoid robots. However, espionage does not necessarily require legs, and the FCC's robot ban is no exception. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's media relations director, confirmed to The Verge that the ban also covers robotic vacuum cleaners. Your existing Roomba at home is not the target of the ban, and companies can continue to import and sell approved models. However, the government claims that future foreign robots will pose a threat to national security, and even robotic vacuum cleaner companies have been suddenly required to commit to manufacturing within the United States.

The FCC stated that advanced robotic devices pose national security risks, and the relevant regulations also apply to seemingly harmless products, such as robotic vacuum cleaners and automatic lawn mowers.

Unless a product receives explicit approval, or is for example manufactured in the United States, it will not be allowed to be sold locally.

The ban is expected to deal a particularly heavy blow to the robotic vacuum cleaner market, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own the relevant products, you can still continue using them today — the FCC will not come to your door to confiscate your robotic vacuum cleaner.

However, depending on how the ban is enforced, the robotic vacuum cleaner market may undergo drastic changes in a short period of time. If you feel this situation seems familiar, that's perfectly normal, because this ban is very similar to the wireless router ban implemented a few months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robotic vacuum cleaner? Why? Feel free to share with us in the comment section.
